sections.skill: Match common insurance categories to risks and read limits and exclusions

questions.prompt: A customer slips on a wet floor in the shop. Which category usually applies?

choices.text: Property coverage for the owner's equipment

questions.intro: Insurance moves some financial risk to an insurer in exchange for a PREMIUM (the price of the policy). Common business categories include GENERAL LIABILITY (injuries or property damage to others, such as a customer slipping), PROFESSIONAL LIABILITY (mistakes in advice or services), PROPERTY (your equipment and inventory), and COMMERCIAL AUTO. Every policy has LIMITS (the most it pays), a DEDUCTIBLE (what you pay first), and EXCLUSIONS (what it does not cover). Read the exclusions and ask a licensed agent which coverage fits your activities.

sections.skill: An umbrella with holes in certain places

questions.prompt: The size of the umbrella stands for what?

choices.text: The premium price of the policy

questions.intro: Insurance is like an umbrella you pay for. It keeps you dry from some kinds of rain, but it is only so big (the limit), you still get a little wet before it opens (the deductible), and it has a few holes in known places (the exclusions). Before a storm, you want to know where the holes are, not discover them while you are getting soaked.
